prompt: A sponsor wants proof that an invoice assistant reduced operating cost. The pilot reports “model response time fell from 11 seconds to 4 seconds,” but invoices still require the same staff correction time. Which outcome belongs in the executive report?

options.text: Report only model speed as evidence of operating-cost savings.
Compare total cost per correct invoice and correction effort.
Claim staff productivity rose because generation is faster.
Report token count instead of total invoice-processing cost.

feedback.reason: Model latency is an operational input, not proof of business productivity when downstream correction is unchanged.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An outcome report links before/after measures to business value and the quality/risk controls that make the comparison meaningful.
details.scenarioApplication: Model latency is an operational input, not proof of business productivity when downstream correction is unchanged.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Use comparable populations and disclose uncertainty or scope limitations; do not infer labor savings from response speed alone.
details.errorCorrection: Match the claim to the measured business outcome, comparison boundary, and evidence quality.
details.transfer: Translate technical metrics into an auditable business result.

messages.text: Response speed measures one component; it does not establish total operating cost or correction savings.
Faster generation does not prove staff time or cost improved across the full invoice workflow.
Tokens can help estimate model spend but omit staff work and correctly completed invoices.

prompt: A deployment chooses between direct API and a customer’s approved cloud route. The sponsor asks for a decision record that will remain useful after the architect leaves. Which artifact is most complete?

options.text: Record provider, unit price, and a general success statement.
Record route rationale and owned, comparable outcome evidence.
Let future sponsors infer business impact from platform metrics.
Report only selected successes without baseline or outcome owner.

feedback.reason: A durable record must support both the route decision and an attributable outcome claim. It needs an accountable owner and comparable before/after measurements with a defined cohort, window, controls, and limits.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A defensible sponsor record links a route/configuration and its rationale to a business measure with the same definition before and after, population/time window, control evidence, and a named owner.
details.scenarioApplication: A durable record must support both the route decision and an attributable outcome claim. It needs an accountable owner and comparable before/after measurements with a defined cohort, window, controls, and limits.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Comparable before/after records support a descriptive change; causal attribution additionally needs a design that addresses competing explanations.
details.errorCorrection: Match the claim to the measured business outcome, comparison boundary, and evidence quality.
details.transfer: Make the record auditable by assigning who will measure, when, on whom, against which baseline and guardrails.

messages.text: Provider choice and a unit price omit decision rationale, outcome baseline, and measurement ownership.
Technical health cannot substitute for the business outcome the sponsor must justify.
Selected successes without a comparable baseline cannot substantiate the stated percentage improvement.

prompt: A pilot claims a 25% reduction in review time based on six hand-picked cases, with no pre-pilot baseline and no record of reviewer overrides. What should the sponsor-facing outcome document say?

options.text: Call the 25% reduction proven because all six cases succeeded.
Omit quality and overrides to simplify the efficiency claim.
Use model speed as proof that human review time improved.
Report the gap; plan a comparable guarded measurement.

feedback.reason: The 25% claim is unsubstantiated without a baseline. Report observed pilot facts and the missing comparison; plan a representative measurement with quality and override evidence.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Business measures need a defined population and guardrails that prevent efficiency from masking quality loss.
details.scenarioApplication: The 25% claim is unsubstantiated without a baseline. Report observed pilot facts and the missing comparison; plan a representative measurement with quality and override evidence.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Small pilot evidence can guide next steps without being presented as a validated impact claim.
details.errorCorrection: Match the claim to the measured business outcome, comparison boundary, and evidence quality.
details.transfer: Make the strength of the claim match the evidence and identify the next measurement.

messages.text: Six selected cases without a baseline cannot establish a 25% reduction in review time.
Omitting overrides can conceal correction effort or quality losses underlying the efficiency claim.
Model latency is not the same quantity as human review time.

prompt: A non-technical sponsor asks whether the AI deployment is “working.” The technical report has p95 latency, context-cache hit rate, and tool timeout percentages, but no user or business measure. What should the architect add?

options.text: Add the business outcome, comparable measures, and evidence limits.
Add more platform metrics; leave business interpretation to the sponsor.
Use a public model benchmark instead of the workflow outcome.
Label success from team confidence after the demo.

feedback.reason: The report must translate technical health into the organization’s business outcome and state the evidence boundaries.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Operational metrics help explain system behavior but do not substitute for the outcome the sponsor asked about.
details.scenarioApplication: The report must translate technical health into the organization’s business outcome and state the evidence boundaries.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep detailed technical evidence available for operators while presenting a concise supported result for the sponsor.
details.errorCorrection: Match the claim to the measured business outcome, comparison boundary, and evidence quality.
details.transfer: Choose the communication artifact for the decision maker while preserving the evidence behind it.

messages.text: More platform metrics still leave the requested business outcome unmeasured.
A public benchmark does not measure change in this organization’s workflow.
Confidence after a demo is not before/after outcome evidence.

prompt: A pilot correctly completes 1,000 invoices in each period, confirmed by review, with the same case mix. Before deployment, total staff and system cost was €5,000. After deployment, staff cost is €4,000 and all system costs are €1,500. What cost result is supported?

options.text: A 20% total saving because staff cost fell by €1,000.
Report a €500 total increase, despite lower staff cost.
A 30% saving because only the new system cost matters.
Zero cost change because invoice volume stayed constant.

feedback.reason: Total cost rises from €5,000 to €5,500, or €5.00 to €5.50 per correctly processed invoice. Staff cost fell, but the full cost boundary shows a 10% increase.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Total cost rises from €5,000 to €5,500, or €5.00 to €5.50 per correctly processed invoice. Staff cost fell, but the full cost boundary shows a 10% increase.
details.scenarioApplication: Total cost rises from €5,000 to €5,500, or €5.00 to €5.50 per correctly processed invoice. Staff cost fell, but the full cost boundary shows a 10% increase.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This describes the stated pilot cost boundary; it does not price unmeasured benefits or future scale.
details.errorCorrection: Separate observed outcomes, attribution, total cost, and mandatory success conditions.
details.transfer: State what changed, the measured scope, and which conditions limit the business claim.

messages.text: The €1,000 staff reduction is offset by €1,500 of system cost; total cost increased.
The system cost must be added to staff cost, not treated as a saving.
Equal volume makes unit comparison possible; it does not make the total costs equal.

prompt: Comparable reporting shows shorter claim-processing time after deployment. During the same period, staffing increased and the claims policy simplified. No control group or other causal adjustment is available. What can the outcome document claim?

options.text: All of the observed improvement was caused by the AI deployment.
The before/after change proves staffing had no effect.
Time improved; the AI contribution remains uncertain.
The observed processing-time measurements must be discarded.

feedback.reason: Report the observed change and concurrent staffing and policy changes. Comparable metric definitions do not isolate the AI contribution from other changes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Report the observed change and concurrent staffing and policy changes. Comparable metric definitions do not isolate the AI contribution from other changes.
details.scenarioApplication: Report the observed change and concurrent staffing and policy changes. Comparable metric definitions do not isolate the AI contribution from other changes.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A stronger causal design may support attribution later; an auditable record alone is not causal identification.
details.errorCorrection: Separate observed outcomes, attribution, total cost, and mandatory success conditions.
details.transfer: State what changed, the measured scope, and which conditions limit the business claim.

messages.text: The comparison does not separate the deployment effect from staffing and policy effects.
There is no evidence here that isolates or rules out the staffing effect.
The measurements remain useful descriptive evidence when their attribution limits are disclosed.

prompt: An assistant reduces average processing time by 18%, but its reviewed serious-error rate exceeds a predeclared quality floor. The sponsor asks to report the pilot as successful because speed improved. What should the report say?

options.text: Report the speed gain and failed quality gate; success is unproven.
Report success and omit errors to keep the executive summary simple.
Average speed and error figures into one score after seeing the results.
Replace the failed floor with a softer target without owner review.

feedback.reason: Disclose both the measured speed improvement and the failed predeclared quality requirement. The gain cannot override a condition that the stated success contract treats as mandatory.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Disclose both the measured speed improvement and the failed predeclared quality requirement. The gain cannot override a condition that the stated success contract treats as mandatory.
details.scenarioApplication: Disclose both the measured speed improvement and the failed predeclared quality requirement. The gain cannot override a condition that the stated success contract treats as mandatory.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The owner may reconsider scope or criteria through an explicit decision; the original pilot still failed its original floor.
details.errorCorrection: Separate observed outcomes, attribution, total cost, and mandatory success conditions.
details.transfer: State what changed, the measured scope, and which conditions limit the business claim.

messages.text: Omitting the failed gate presents incomplete evidence and hides the condition preventing the success claim.
A post-hoc combined score changes the success rule and can trade away the mandatory quality floor.
Changing the requirement requires its authorized owner and a transparent revised decision, not silent relabeling.
